# ENV012: Configured proxy did not accept a connection

<!-- Code generated by cmd/rulegen from the builtin registry. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Component: network. Severity: info.

Collector prerequisites: proxy.

The configured proxy endpoint refused the bounded TCP connection or had no reachable network route.

Evidence required: An explicitly requested probe of a configured proxy endpoint returned connection refusal or no-route evidence.

Manual steps:

- Check the configured proxy host/port and local network or VPN, then repeat the opt-in probe.

Verify with `envdoctor diagnose --rule ENV012 --probe-network`.

Limitations:

- Default diagnosis records only redacted configuration and leaves reachability untested.
- --probe-network allows at most three configured endpoints, one DNS lookup/one TCP dial each, and a one-second total deadline.
- No credentials, application bytes, external HTTP requests or TLS handshakes are sent; connections are closed.
- DNS failure, denial, timeout, cancellation and invalid URLs remain unknown/degraded. NO_PROXY is recorded only as configured/unconfigured.
- Use ASCII/punycode hostnames or unscoped IPv6 literals. Zone-qualified IPv6 endpoints and unsupported URL schemes are degraded configuration.

No command is executed by this rule. Evidence comes only from the snapshot. Failed prerequisite collectors disable the rule. Positive, negative and edge fixtures cover Windows, Linux and macOS; platform exclusions are listed above.

Documentation: <https://github.com/shellghostt/envdoctor/blob/main/docs/rules/ENV012.md>.
